negative_findings.description: UniCredit does not operate a separate Slovak bank: the Slovak business has run since 1 December 2013 as an organisational unit (pobocka zahranicnej banky) of UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia, a.s., domiciled in Prague. No standalone SK segment P&L was found at either the Prague entity or UniCredit Group level.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only combined CZ+SK figures located (e.g. group net profit CZK 5,853m at 30 June 2024); no SK-only split found in the reports reached.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any 'Slovakia' market share or profitability series built from parent disclosures will have a structural hole for UniCredit; SK-only UniCredit figures must come from NBS aggregate statistics or the SK organisational unit's local filings instead.

negative_findings.description: J&T Finance Group SE and PPF are privately held and run no conventional investor-relations site with quarterly presentations; disclosure is limited to annual (and for J&T, semi-annual) statutory/bond-issuer reports plus press releases, largely in Czech/Slovak.
negative_findings.result_summary: Found consolidated annual reports (JTFG SE 2024 PDF; PPF Group annual accounts 2022/2024/2025) but no quarterly segment reporting, no results presentations, no fact books.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The domestically-controlled part of the SK banking market (J&T Banka SK, 365.bank, Postova banka; Home Credit SK) will be observable only at annual frequency and with far less granularity than Erste/KBC/RBI/Intesa units — a permanent asymmetry in any quarterly SK market model.

negative_findings.description: Slovak-language searching for the parent-IR channel itself (queries using 'materska skupina', 'prezentacia pre investorov', 'segment Slovensko', 'stvrtrocne vysledky') returned almost no parent-published Slovak material.
negative_findings.result_summary: SK queries surfaced subsidiary annual reports, SK/CZ trade press and aggregators (finstat.sk, teraz.sk, patria.cz, e15.cz, kurzy.cz) rather than parent IR pages. Parents publish this channel in English (and German/Italian/Dutch), not Slovak.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms a structural rule for this cell: local-language crawling is the wrong instrument for parent IR. SK terms are still essential for the subsidiary mirrors and for SK/CZ media that relay parent numbers, so both language tracks must be kept but pointed at different targets.

negative_findings.description: Several parents serve report files from cache-busting or hashed CDN paths that cannot be templated: KBC (wcmassets.kbc.be/.../<file>.pdf.cdn.res/last-modified/<epoch>/<file>.pdf), RBI (*.coredownload.pdf/.xlsm), PPF (datocms-assets.com/<id>/<epoch>-<name>.pdf), J&T (kc-usercontent.com GUID paths).
negative_findings.result_summary: Direct file URLs observed in search results, but each embeds a timestamp or GUID that changes on republication.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector that hardcodes these URLs will silently rot. Link resolution must always start from the HTML index page, and stored URLs should be treated as snapshots, not durable identifiers.

negative_findings.description: No URL in this slice is claimed as verified-live. Only three pages were actually fetched in this pass (Erste financial-reports index, RBI reports page, Intesa subsidiaries-annual-reports page); all others come from search-result metadata.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Liveness, robots/ToS posture and bot-defence behaviour for the remaining domains (kbc.com, group.intesasanpaolo.com deep PDFs, ppf.eu, jtbanka.sk, unicreditbank.cz/sk, ftp.pse.cz, finstat.sk) are unverified hypotheses for the deterministic verification pass.

coverage_gaps.description: 365.bank is mid-transition: KBC announced acquisition of ~98.45% from the J&T side. Its disclosure channel will migrate from J&T Finance Group's annual report to KBC's International Markets/Slovakia quarterly line, and the handover date and treatment (when it enters KBC's Slovakia segment; KBC's 2Q2026 Slovakia result already flags EUR 16m from 'recent acquisitions') were not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Track KBC IR closing/completion announcements and the first quarterly report in which 365.bank is consolidated; keep the J&T annual report in scope for pre-closing history and build an explicit before/after continuity note so the SK series is not broken by the reclassification.

coverage_gaps.description: Regulated-news / ad-hoc disclosure feeds of the parents (Vienna Stock Exchange and OeKB for Erste and RBI, Euronext Brussels/STORI for KBC, Borsa Italiana/eMarket SDIR-Storage for Intesa) were not searched. These carry the legally definitive, timestamped version of results and M&A announcements — often before the IR website is updated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a dedicated discovery pass for the national officially-appointed mechanisms (OAMs) and exchange news services covering AT, BE, IT issuers, and register the machine-readable ESEF/XBRL filings there.

coverage_gaps.description: ESEF/XBRL structured annual filings and Pillar 3 / country-by-country reporting (CRD Art. 89) were not scouted. CBCR is the one parent disclosure that legally mandates a per-country breakout — turnover, profit before tax, tax paid, employees for Slovakia — for every one of Erste, RBI, KBC, Intesa and UniCredit, on a fully comparable basis.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a targeted pass for each parent's Pillar 3 / CBCR annex and ESEF filing packages; CBCR gives an apples-to-apples SK country series that survives segment redefinitions and covers UniCredit's otherwise invisible SK unit.

coverage_gaps.description: Smaller SK banks with foreign parents were outside the named cell list and were not scouted: mBank (Commerzbank-linked, SK branch), Oberbank AG SK branch, BKS Bank SK, ING Bank N.V. SK branch, Citibank Europe plc SK branch, Fio banka SK, Komercni banka's SK branch, and consumer-finance arms (BNP Paribas Personal Finance/Cetelem, Home Credit SK).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the cell in a follow-up pass to branch-model banks whose only disclosure is at foreign-parent level; note most publish nothing SK-specific, so CBCR and NBS branch statistics will be the practical substitutes.

coverage_gaps.description: Earnings-call transcripts, Q&A audio/webcasts and analyst pre-consensus were identified as existing (Erste audio/video webcasts, KBC replay webinars and sell-side preconsensus) but not scouted as sources in their own right. Analyst Q&A is where parents are pressed on the Slovak bank levy, mortgage repricing and competitive response — detail absent from written reports.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout transcript/webcast sources (issuer webcast archives first; third-party transcript aggregators noted separately with licensing caveats) and treat Slovakia-tagged Q&A exchanges as a distinct evidence type.

coverage_gaps.description: Parent-language (non-English) IR editions were not scouted: German for Erste/RBI, Italian for Intesa, Dutch for KBC. These sometimes publish earlier, and Italian/Dutch releases occasionally carry subsidiary detail trimmed from the English edition.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add DE/IT/NL query variants (e.g. 'Segment Slowakei', 'controllate estere Slovacchia', 'Internationale Markten Slowakije') in a follow-up pass and compare against the English editions for content deltas.

brief: Because Slovakia's systemic banks are subsidiaries, the densest quantitative disclosure about them is published abroad and in English: Erste (Slovakia segment, with a machine-readable Key Financials XLSX each quarter), KBC (an explicit Slovakia net-result line inside International Markets, quarterly), RBI (Slovakia country segment plus an XLSM results workbook), and Intesa (a year-by-year archive of VUB's full annual reports hosted on the parent's own IR site). These four are the backbone of the cell and are all crawlable, high-credibility, regularly scheduled, and partly tabular. Coverage degrades sharply outside them: J&T Finance Group and PPF are private and disclose only annually in Czech/Slovak, and UniCredit has no Slovak segment at all because the SK business is a branch of a Prague-domiciled entity. Slovak-language search proved the wrong instrument for this channel — it surfaces subsidiary mirrors and SK/CZ trade press rather than parent IR — and the biggest untapped opportunity is CRD Art. 89 country-by-country reporting, the one mandated per-country breakout that would cover every parent, including UniCredit, on a comparable basis.
